glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: spec
  Severity: high
  File: shared/tests/test_supabase_nextjs_rules_drift.py (FIXTURE constant / BLOCKS map)
  Finding: The drift test depends on a committed fixture tree at `shared/tests/fixtures/supabase_nextjs_scaffold/` containing every mapped example file (16 mapped blocks + 1 whole file), but the diff contains no fixture files. The acceptance criterion "Committed fixture tree built from the templates' own examples passes every mechanical rule" cannot be met by this diff alone — the suite will fail with `FileNotFoundError` on a fresh checkout unless the fixtures were committed in a separate change not shown here.
  Suggestion: Commit the fixture tree in this change (or point to the commit that adds it); verify the test suite passes end-to-end from a clean clone.

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: shared/tests/test_supabase_nextjs_rules_drift.py — `_lint` / `no-restricted-globals` branch
  Finding: The emulation strips comments but not string literals, so `const s = "no fetch here"` in a component would be flagged as a `fetch` violation. This only produces false positives inside the test (not shipped ESLint), but it means the drift test could report a spurious failure for a template example that mentions `fetch` in prose-in-strings, and the "compliant" tests never cover that case.
  Suggestion: Either strip string literals before the global-name search, or accept and document the divergence; add a negative test for a string containing "fetch".

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: shared/tests/test_supabase_nextjs_rules_drift.py — `_imports`
  Finding: The test comment claims "`import type` counts (the core rule flags it too)", but this is asserted rather than verified. In real ESLint, `no-restricted-imports` pattern matching with `importNames` historically did not flag `import type` declarations the same way (type-only imports were excluded from import-name checks in several ESLint versions). If the emulator is stricter than real ESLint, a future real-ESLint run (the stated replacement) could silently disagree with the drift test in the permissive direction — which is the dangerous direction.
  Suggestion: Verify against a real ESLint run once (the planned unit) that `import type { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'` is actually flagged; if not, the rule text "must not import createClient" needs a lint pattern that covers type imports, or the note should scope the guarantee.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: shared/profiles/supabase-nextjs.json — `supabase-client-through-helpers` `ignores`
  Finding: The ignore list omits `**/*.stories.*` and dev-only patterns, but more importantly the `files` glob `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs}` combined with ignoring only `src/lib/supabase/**` means `src/middleware.ts` (the standard place a Next.js Supabase SSR project refreshes sessions via `@supabase/ssr`) is in scope and must use an eslint-disable. This is defensible but the note doesn't mention middleware, which is the most common legitimate hit.
  Suggestion: Either add `src/middleware.*` to ignores or document it in the note as a per-line-disable case.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: shared/profiles/supabase-nextjs.json — `no-fetch-in-components` `files`
  Finding: `src/app/**/*.{tsx,jsx}` excludes `.ts` files under `src/app/`, so a `src/app/some-layout-helper.ts` or a custom `src/app/*.ts` module that calls `fetch()` escapes the rule. The note explains route.ts exclusion but not the broader `.ts` gap under `src/app/`.
  Suggestion: Consider `src/app/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}` with an explicit ignore for `**/route.ts` if the intent is "route handlers excluded, everything else under app/ covered" — or document the current scope precisely.

Test quality is otherwise good: seeded-violation and compliant/exempt parameterized tests exercise real behavior, unknown-rule emulation fails loudly, and the fixture-equality tests pin template drift.

## Overall assessment

The profile and template changes are sound and well-tested, but the acceptance criterion "committed fixture tree" is not visible in this diff — if the fixtures are genuinely absent the whole suite fails. Ship-with-fixes after confirming/committing the fixtures and resolving the `import type` emulation-vs-ESLint question.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
